seven the Sahara desert is just sand when people picture the Sahara they see
endless sand dunes but sand only covers about 25% of the Sahara most of it is
actually rocky plateaus, gravel plains, and mountains. The sand dune image comes from
movies and postcards, but it's not what most of the Sahara actually looks like.
Number six, the Red Sea is red. The Red Sea has red right in the name, so the water must be red,
right? The water is actually blue like any other sea. The name comes from seasonal algae blooms
that sometimes create reddish patches, but 99% of the time it looks like normal blue ocean water.
Number five, Alaska is huge compared to other countries. Speaking of map lies, Alaska looks
enormous on most maps, bigger than Brazil or Australia. Brazil is five times bigger
than Alaska, and Australia is four times bigger. The same map distortion that makes Greenland
look massive also makes Alaska look like a giant when it's actually much smaller than
you think.
Number four. The Caspian Sea is a sea, and it's salty like an ocean, but it's actually
the world's largest lake. It's completely surrounded by land, with no connection to
any ocean. We just call it a sea because it's so big and salty. But geographically, it's
a lake.
Number 3. Rivers always flow north.
to south. This seems logical because we think of north as up and south as down on maps.
But rivers flow downhill and downhill can be in any direction. The Nile flows north,
the Mississippi flows south, the Amazon flows east. Rivers don't care about your map directions,
they just follow gravity. Number two. Holland and the Netherlands are the same thing.
millions of people think Holland is a country. It's not. Holland is just one
region inside the Netherlands. Calling the whole country Holland is like
calling all of America Texas. Some Dutch people actually get annoyed when you do
this. So now you know better. Number one. Africa is mostly in the southern
hemisphere. Look at most maps and Africa seems like it's mostly below the
equator. Wrong again. Almost two-thirds of Africa is actually in the northern hemisphere.
Countries like Egypt, Libya, Algeria, and most of Nigeria are all north of the equator.
